idea: VoyaGreen finds travelers a lower-pressure place with the same vibe, then plans the trip. It scores a destination's tourism pressure from environmental and crowding indicators, suggests a greener alternative when it's overcrowded, and builds a day-by-day itinerary from the traveler's interests and trip length.
who: Filipino tourists planning a local trip use it to pick a place that is as good as the famous one, without adding to the crowding and strain on it.
core: The pressure check and swap: pick a destination, see its tourism-pressure score with the indicators behind it, and get a greener alternative with a personalized itinerary.
demo: Open VoyaGreen: quick onboarding, then pick beach, food and snorkeling for a 3-day trip
Tap Boracay: its tourism-pressure score is High (87), with the indicators behind it and a greener pick with the same vibe, Carabao Island
Tap Carabao Island: a 3-day itinerary built on those interests, 58 points lower pressure, saved to My trips
pain: Every traveler gets sent to the same few famous spots, so those places get overcrowded and strained, and nobody sees the pressure their choice adds.
painPoints: Recommendations rank by popularity, price and distance, never by the pressure on the place
Sustainability data exists but is scattered, and nobody checks it before choosing a trip
Lesser-known places with the same vibe stay invisible
hook: Kyla has three days, a barkada, and one question: where do we go? Every app she opens gives her the same answer — the place everyone else is already going.
character: Kyla, a college student in Quezon City planning her barkada's summer trip, who books Boracay because it is the first thing every TikTok and travel site shows her
closer: VoyaGreen won't tell you to stay home. It shows you somewhere just as good that the crowd hasn't found. Travel greener, not less.
how: Pick a place, your days and your interests. VoyaGreen scores its tourism pressure, shows the indicators behind it, and if it's High, swaps in a same-vibe place and builds your itinerary there.
hardPart: making the swap feel like the same trip: same vibe, and every day built from your own interests
pitch30: Travel apps send everyone to the same famous places, and those places pay for it. VoyaGreen checks a destination's tourism pressure before you go. If it's crowded, it finds a lower-pressure place with the same vibe and builds your itinerary there. Same great trip, less strain.

qa.q: Where does the pressure score come from?
qa.a: In this demo the scores are seeded and illustrative, and the app labels them demo data. Each one combines visitor density, carrying-capacity use, environmental strain and peak-season crowding. The real version would pull those indicators from public tourism-arrival and environmental data.
No. In this MVP it's assembled from a curated activity list per destination, matched to your interests and trip length. There's no live AI call, so it never fails on stage.
There are only five seeded Philippine destinations, the scores are illustrative rather than measured, and there's no live data feed, no booking, no accounts and no real map. Those are next.

qa.q: Won't this just move the crowd to the alternative?
qa.a: It could, and that's the right worry. It isn't built yet, but crowd rotation is next on our list: once scores are live, alternatives rotate as their own pressure rises, so we spread visitors out instead of relocating the crowd.
